evaluations.note: 16 on the reference machine since the neighbour lists are exact (2026-09-30; 17 after the sheared cells of common/data/elastic.tadahdb were corrected, 30 before that, 16 with the previous 15-digit scripts). Since common/lammps/Ecoh_param.in switched to exact captures, HPO reads Ecoh, Eiso and Ebulk and the relaxed lattice constant back without rounding, which exposes the ~1e-13 relative re-evaluation noise of the warm-started lattice relaxation. BFGS reaches the upper bound RCUT2B = 6.0 at eval 9 (the best, 1.031156e-01) and from eval 13 on its line search re-evaluates the clamped bound; whether its sufficient-decrease test passes there depends on the sign of that noise. Here it passes after the re-evaluations at the bound (evals 13-14) and BFGS ends after its finite-difference pair (evals 15-16); when it never passes, the run continues to MAXEVAL (30), as example 01's identical search does on the reference machine, and a 1-ulp change of the hot_a0 start or of one training energy decides which. So the count is not pinned (evals_tol 14: 2..30, see tolerance_rationale); the status stays COMPLETED in every case, and best loss, components and RCUT2B do not depend on it.

tolerance_rationale: Best loss, components and RCUT2B are pinned at the default tolerances. The evaluation count is not deterministic across machines: the optimum is on the clamped bound RCUT2B = 6.0 (eval 9), and whether DLIB:BFGS's line search accepts a re-evaluation there depends on the sign of a ~1e-13 relative, rounding-level drift of the warm-started lattice relaxation. The run stops after 16 evaluations on the reference machine (with exact neighbour lists, 2026-09-30; 17 before) or runs to MAXEVAL = 30 (as example 01 does with the same search), and a 1-ulp change of the hot_a0 start or of one training energy flips it; evals_tol 14 accepts 2..30.
